Hi Elliot — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a few questions so we can confirm the commercial path and procurement readiness: 

Recap:
- Demo: basic flow validated (billing account -> Dedicated trial -> production).
- Questions remaining: AP acceptance (PO vs card), vendor onboarding (W-9/PO templates), and marketplace (AWS/GCP listing interest).

Questions for you:
1) Does SkyFoundry require a PO for any contract > $10k/year, or is a corporate card acceptable with a PO only for >$50k?
2) Who on your AP team manages new vendor setup — can we loop that person in?
3) Any blocking vendor policies (e.g., only domestic vendors, vendor classification, or tax form requirements) that would prevent Redwood from being paid by card?

Next steps I propose:
- If PO required: we’ll send a filled PO template and the SOC2 + SOW packet for legal.
- If card acceptable: provide invoice cadence + remittance details and confirm card processor (we accept ACH/credit card).

Attachments: SkyFoundry_PO_template.pdf (blank PO for your procurement), Redwood-commercial-summary.xlsx (pricing tiers & committed capacity options).

If you prefer, Marissa can run a short procurement checklist call with your AP team (15m). What time works on Tue/Wed?

Thanks Sofia — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- PO policy: Our default is PO for any vendor engagement with annual spend >= $25k. Card payments are allowed for ad-hoc/one-off invoices under $5k, but corporate cards are tightly controlled and routed through procurement.
- Vendor onboarding: AP requires a W-9 (we’re US entity), vendor bank details for ACH, and our vendor risk team requires SOC2 or equivalent for SaaS vendors that store/process customer data.
- Blocking items: We are restricted on foreign payment processors (we prefer US-based merchant accounts). If Redwood processes credit cards through an international gateway, that could be a blocker.

I’m copying AP (ap@skyfoundry.com) and Dana (Finance) — AP can confirm what version of the PO template is needed. 

Elliot
Head of Partnerships | SkyFoundry
elliot@skyfoundry.com

Hi Elliot / AP team — Marissa here on the commercial ops side. Appreciate the clear PO thresholds. A couple of items from our side to speed onboarding: 

1) If PO is required for >= $25k, we can support a 12-month reserved Dedicated plan that sits below that threshold for a pilot phase (or we can go PDQ with a PO and commit). We can also price a one-off pilot that’s card-friendly under $5k.
2) Attached is a pre-filled PO template (SkyFoundry_PO_template.pdf) with our EIN and remit-to details filled — please confirm which PO number format you need so we can return a signed copy quickly.
3) On the merchant processor question: Redwood can bill via ACH and wire directly to our US Treasury account. For credit card payments we route through Stripe (US-based). If you need an on-prem merchant account, let's surface that as a potential blocker.

Quick ask: can AP confirm whether Stripe-supported card payments are acceptable for vendor onboarding, or if you need us to invoice and remit via ACH only? If ACH is preferred, we’ll note that as default and include wiring instructions in the SOW.

Available for a 15m procurement checklist call tomorrow 10:30–11:30 PT or Wednesday 14:00–16:00 PT. Let me know what works and I’ll send a calendar invite.

Best,

Hi Marissa — thanks for the follow-up and for the pre-filled PO. Quick answers from AP: 

- Stripe (US) is acceptable for processing card payments — please provide the Stripe merchant summary page or a demo statement showing Redwood’s US routing.
- For onboarding we need: completed PO (signed by SkyFoundry), W-9, and remit-to banking info (ACH).
- If you prefer to keep the pilot under $5k and bill to card, that is simplest for timing. If you want to proceed with a PO for a longer pilot, please return the signed PO and we’ll create the vendor record (this can take 5–7 business days).

We have a standing 15m slot daily at 10:30 PT for vendor checklist calls — please send an invite if that works.
